citations.quote: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

association_citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

With no cross-candidate computation performed in this task, no evidence-based recommendation of C4 over the additive branch is justified, so the decision is held.

The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

evidence_ledger.quote: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

evidence_ledger.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

citations.quote: Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

requirements.reasoning: The paper reports hard carbon (HC) anodes paired with NFM cathodes in the pouch cells.

In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

association_citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

requirements.reasoning: The paper reports hard carbon (HC) anodes paired with NFM cathodes in the pouch cells.

citations.quote: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

association_citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：C1-NaFSI-NaPF6-dualsalt。

### 候选资料：C1-NaFSI-NaPF6-dualsalt（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；总盐浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaFSI：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, PC, EMC, DEC；溶剂比例（质量）：DEC=1.0, EC=1.0, EMC=6.0, PC=2.0。
- 配方原文 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]：Ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), $NaPF_{6}$ and NaFSI used in the electrolyte are all from the commercial products of Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. and not further purified. The blank electrolyte was a mixture of 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC, PC, EMC and DEC with a ratio of 1:2:6:1 (by weight). NaFSI was added to the blank electrolyte to replace part of $NaPF_{6}$ , maintaining the total content of NaFSI and $NaPF_{6}$ at 1 M. In this work, "blank" represents 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ , "0.1 M NaFSI" represents 0.1 M $NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.3 M NaFSI" represents 0.3 M $NaFSI + 0.7 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.5 M NaFSI" represents 0.5 M $NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.7 M NaFSI" represents 0.7 M $NaFSI + 0.3 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.9 M NaFSI" represents 0.9 M $NaFSI + 0.1 M NaPF_{6}$ . All electrolytes were prepared in an argon-filled glove box with $H_{2}O$ and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm.

## 候选评估
### C1-NaFSI-NaPF6-dualsalt
评估建议：The candidate's salt identity, concentrations, solvent ratios (mass basis), cell format, voltage window and -20 C 0.5 C/1 C target rates all match the paper's directly tested 0.5 M NaFSI dual-salt branch, which reports improved low-temperature discharge capacity, so the literature supports recommending this candidate.

[0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]

[0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
